title: Trapdoor Hiding in Lookup-Table-Based Designs
summary: All reported attempts to hide a trapdoor in lookup-table-based designs failed; it remains to prove impossibility given state-of-the-art preimage-resistant-function design or exhibit a counterexample.

formal_statement.body: All attempts to hide a trapdoor in lookup-table-based designs have failed. Determine whether, given the state of the art in the design of preimage-resistant functions, every lookup-table-based scheme necessarily fails to hide a trapdoor; prove this conjectured impossibility or refute it by exhibiting a scheme that does hide one.

scope.domain: Design of lookup-table-based cryptographic schemes with hidden trapdoors.
assumptions: The claimed impossibility is considered given the state of the art in designing preimage-resistant functions.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove that every lookup-table-based scheme fails to hide a trapdoor under the stated limitation, or refute the conjecture by exhibiting a scheme that hides one.

citations.label: Cryptographic Schemes Based on the ASASA Structure: Black-Box, White-Box, and Public-Key (Extended Abstract)

progress.summary: The source reports that all attempts so far had failed and explicitly conjectures that no lookup-table-based scheme can hide a trapdoor, at least given the state of the art in designing preimage-resistant functions.
citation_labels: Alex Biryukov et al., Cryptographic Schemes Based on the ASASA Structure: Black-Box, White-Box, and Public-Key (Extended Abstract)
